findings.message: The gitignore inversion exposes nothing that exists: zero newly-visible untracked files under either inverted tree, and the two scratch classes the old catch-all actually protected stay hidden.
findings.detail_md:
Verified by probe rather than by reading the claim. `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- specs/releases specs/_archive` is empty, and `git check-ignore` confirms the surviving narrow ignores still fire at any depth:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `specs/releases/<id>/local-notes.md` | IGNORED |
| `specs/releases/<id>/tmp/scratch.txt` | IGNORED |
| `specs/_archive/releases/<id>/local-notes.md` | IGNORED |
| `specs/releases/<id>/verdicts/<sha>.handoff.json` | TRACKABLE (the point of the fix) |

Structurally this is the right shape: one negation replaces a catch-all plus ~20 per-artifact opt-ins, so no future canonical artifact class needs a fifth whitelist line. The contract test pins both directions, including this bug's own regression seam.

findings.message: Defence-in-depth note on the inversion: inside specs/releases/** and specs/_archive/releases/**, sensitive file classes that the old catch-all incidentally hid (.env, *.pem, *.key, caches, a nested .dadaia/) are now trackable, because a later negation wins over the earlier global ignores.
findings.detail_md:
Probed: under a release directory, `.env`, `.env.local`, `server.pem`, `creds.key`, `.coverage`, `__pycache__/x.pyc` and `.dadaia/state.json` all report TRACKABLE, where the pre-inversion catch-all would have ignored them. Root-level `.env`, `.env.local`, `secrets.pem` and `.coverage` are unaffected and remain IGNORED.

No instance exists: nothing of that shape is present anywhere under either tree, credentials live in the workspace-root `.env` by law (never inside a repo's specs tree), and three content-based backstops remain in force — the pre-push denylist scan (which reads every new object's content, including a `secret-token` baseline pattern), the gitleaks CI job, and the repo self-scan. So this is a prospective reduction in defence in depth, not an exposure, and it does not gate the release.

Recorded for the fix owner rather than actioned here because the remedy must not undo the inversion: gitignore is last-match-wins, so re-asserting the sensitive classes in one trailing block after the negation restores the protection without reintroducing the per-artifact opt-in shape the inversion exists to kill.
findings.fix_recommendation: PM intake, not an rc-1 fix: append one trailing block re-ignoring the sensitive classes (`**/.env*`, `**/*.pem`, `**/*.key`, `**/__pycache__/`, `**/.coverage`, `**/.dadaia/`) after the release-tree negation, and extend the existing hygiene contract test with those probes. One block, one test - never a per-artifact line.
